follow-up time: retrospective review over 27 years, with some participants followed up until >2 years old
cohort: 416 infants with Down syndrome hospitalized in a neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) over a 27-year period
finding: Infants with Down syndrome born prematurely, particularly those born before 34 weeks gestation, experience high mortality rates, with a significant proportion of survivors developing moderate to severe cerebral palsy.
mod_finding: Most infants with Down syndrome born at <34 weeks' gestation are born by cesarean section because of the non-reassuring fetal status.
